key_insight: Nb and Ta preferentially segregate to (Hf,Ta,Ti,Nb,Zr)B₂ grain boundaries, linking lower boundary energies and favorable Fermi-level bonding to stronger interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Controlling grain-boundary chemistry could improve the mechanical performance of high-entropy diboride ceramics.
method: DFT calculations of four grain-boundary types in five binary diborides and HEB₂.
COHP analysis of metal–boron bonding at grain boundaries.
Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics sampling of six HEB₂ boundaries using a fine-tuned MACE potential.
evidence_signal: Nb and Ta enriched at five of six HEB₂ boundaries to reported concentrations of 23–35 at.% at 2000 K; a segregated Σ193 boundary sustained 26 GPa versus 20 GPa for a random boundary at 300 K.
watch_item: The computational findings require experimental validation, and the reported strength gain for one boundary may not generalize to bulk polycrystalline ceramics.
paper_title: Instability-driven segregation of V group transition metals on HEB$_2$ grain boundaries influencing enhanced mechanical properties
